READY
The bug is in `com.google.javascript.jscomp.SourceFile.getLine(int)`.

Diagnosis:
- `JSCompilerSourceExcerptProviderTest.testExceptNoNewLine()` expects the last line of a file to be returned even when the file does not end with `\n`.
- `Compiler.getSourceLine(...)` delegates to `SourceFile.getLine(...)`.
- `JsMessageExtractorTest.testSyntaxError1/2()` also depend on this behavior through `LightweightMessageFormatter`, which only includes the source excerpt if `getSourceLine(...)` returns a non-null line.

Static evidence:
- In `SourceFile.getLine(int)`, after finding the start offset of the requested line, it does:

  - if `js.indexOf('\n', pos) == -1`, comment says:
    1. return `null` if `pos` is already at EOF
    2. otherwise return contents from `pos` to end of file

  - but the implementation unconditionally does `return null;`

So valid final lines without trailing newline are lost.

Dynamic verification confirmed:
- On a failing scenario, runtime reaches the branch where no subsequent newline exists for a valid line, and the method returns `null` instead of the substring from `pos` to end of file.

- `provider.getSourceLine("foo2", 3)` returns `null` instead of `"foo2:third line"`.
- Error formatting in `JsMessageExtractorTest` omits the offending source line because `sourceExcerpt == null`.

Root cause:
- Incorrect logic in the no-next-newline case of `SourceFile.getLine(int)`.

Expected fix shape:
- When `js.indexOf('\n', pos) == -1`, return `null` only if `pos >= js.length()`;
- otherwise return `js.substring(pos)`.

READY
The bug is in `com.google.javascript.jscomp.SourceFile.getLine(int)`.

Diagnosis:
- `JSCompilerSourceExcerptProviderTest.testExceptNoNewLine()` expects the last line of a file to be returned even when the file does not end with `\n`.
- `Compiler.getSourceLine(...)` delegates to `SourceFile.getLine(...)`.
- `JsMessageExtractorTest.testSyntaxError1/2()` also depend on this behavior through `LightweightMessageFormatter`, which only includes the source excerpt if `getSourceLine(...)` returns a non-null line.

Static evidence:
- In `SourceFile.getLine(int)`, after finding the start offset of the requested line, it does:

  - if `js.indexOf('\n', pos) == -1`, comment says:
    1. return `null` if `pos` is already at EOF
    2. otherwise return contents from `pos` to end of file

  - but the implementation unconditionally does `return null;`

So valid final lines without trailing newline are lost.

Dynamic verification confirmed:
- On a failing scenario, runtime reaches the branch where no subsequent newline exists for a valid line, and the method returns `null` instead of the substring from `pos` to end of file.

Why this explains all failures:
- `provider.getSourceLine("foo2", 3)` returns `null` instead of `"foo2:third line"`.
- Error formatting in `JsMessageExtractorTest` omits the offending source line because `sourceExcerpt == null`.

Root cause:
- Incorrect logic in the no-next-newline case of `SourceFile.getLine(int)`.

Expected fix shape:
- When `js.indexOf('\n', pos) == -1`, return `null` only if `pos >= js.length()`;
- otherwise return `js.substring(pos)`.
